novelty_flags.label: Open-ended Question 1 / ChenDarwiche2024 comparison
novelty_flags.one_line: The claimed “strict extension” is inaccurate: Theorem 18 assumes positivity for each treatment variable, whereas requiring positive mass for every joint treatment assignment is stronger, so the proposed support regime is not a strict superset.

novelty_flags.label: Proposition 1
novelty_flags.one_line: Both proposed models make the observed outcome Y constant almost surely, so the closure counterexample is degenerate rather than a generic nondegenerate obstruction.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 5
novelty_flags.one_line: After imposing a fixed positive-support face, the result is the ordinary multinomial CLT plus the smooth delta method and standard plug-in Wald argument.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 9, Theorem 18; pp. 20–22, proof of Theorem 18
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 18 uses the constraint set {Pr(X)>0, X in treatment variables}; its converse proof constructs a replacement parent state as a Cartesian product.
Theorem 6.1 states soundness: whenever IDENTIFY+ returns a positivity condition and identification formula, they are correct.
ID is sound and complete; failure yields a hedge and the hedge criterion characterizes identification.
The paper proves NP-hardness of CSI nonidentifiability and supplies a provably sound CSI calculus/search procedure.
The complete algorithm is restricted to CSI relations on observed nodes having no parents.
Discrete causal problems are reduced to polynomial programs and the method computes sharp bounds, including point-identified cases.
The delta method transfers weak convergence, including asymptotic normality, through a differentiable finite-dimensional map.

The accessible preprint presents arithmetic-circuit constrained identification and says it is at least as complete as classical strict-positivity methods; the claimed AAAI proceedings version was not located for theorem-number verification.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace “strictly extend” Chen--Darwiche Theorem 18 with an explicitly non-comparable fixed-alphabet/joint-support regime, or prove a true inclusion by weakening the positivity domain while retaining alphabet preservation.

Replace the closure counterexample by a positive-dimensional binary family with nonconstant observed Y and full nondegenerate observed support, while preserving equal observed laws and distinct joint-intervention outcomes.

State an output language that permits algebraic certificate parameters, or prove that the fixed-alphabet identified functional is always support-guarded rational; this resolves the stated irrational-fiber limitation before claiming completeness.

recommended_next_step: Revise the comparator-domain claim and nondegenerate closure witness, then retain the guarded fixed-alphabet dichotomy as the field-level Stage 0 target.
